key_insight: The paper shows that augmenting Isabelle-based theorem proving with retrieval, error tracing, and counterexample generation can improve automated formal verification of blockchain consensus protocols.
engineering_relevance: This work points to a practical path for making formal verification more accessible and efficient for safety- and security-critical distributed systems such as blockchain consensus.
method: Built an enhanced IsabeLLM pipeline for automated theorem proving in Isabelle.
Added Retrieval-Augmented Generation to provide the LLM with better proof context.
Implemented error tracing, counterexample generation, and updated Isabelle/Sledgehammer compatibility.
evidence_signal: The authors compare the original and improved IsabeLLM versions on verification of Bitcoin’s Proof of Work consensus, using successful completion of that proof task as the evaluation target.
watch_item: The reported improvement is centered on a specific consensus verification case, so broader generalization to other protocols or theorem-proving tasks may still need validation.
paper_title: IsabeLLM: Automated Theorem Proving Applied to Formally Verifying Consensus
